title.narrative: Start Fund Nepal

description.narrative: Key assumptions for Phase III (2025-26): a) Crises occur that are relevant to the Start Fund Nepal niche and alerts are raised by member agencies. b) Decision-making is unbiased and driven by affected population needs over organisational benefit. c) SFN members prioritise decision-making meetings and are available on time. d) Familiarity and confidence in the Start Fund mechanism (standard and anticipation windows) is maintained. e) Speed of fund distribution to accounts is sustained. f) Timely raising of alert notes and availability of data/insight. g) SFN awarded agencies can access project intervention areas. h) Political conflict, elections, festival time and other risks do not significantly impact response timing. i) Federal, provincial and local government support and provide a favourable environment for effective response. j) LNNGOs complete due diligence assessments, are operational in alert areas, and submit proposals when the fund is activated. k) Donors are interested and have available funding to support the pooled funding mechanism.

Start Fund Nepal (SFN) is a rapid response and anticipatory humanitarian financing mechanism that enables timely, locally-led responses to under-the-radar and forecastable crises in Nepal. Operating under the Start Network, SFN pools funding from donors to activate grants within 72 hours of an alert, supporting member organisations — including local and national NGOs (LNNGOs) — to respond to floods, landslides, heatwaves, coldwaves, droughts and other hazards. The fund prioritises speed, community accountability, and localisation, ensuring affected and at-risk populations receive timely, needs-driven assistance while building the humanitarian system's anticipatory capacity through FOREWARN.
